# 🎯 Dynatrace Intelligence: Agentic & Generative AI — Hands-On Workshop

---

Welcome to the **Dynatrace Intelligence AI Hands-On Workshop**! In this session, you will learn how to leverage Dynatrace's built-in AI capabilities to accelerate troubleshooting, query data using natural language, and scale your team's operational knowledge.

## Workshop Agenda

| # | Module | Duration |
|---|--------|----------|
| 1 | **The Troubleshooting Assistant** — Navigating Dynatrace Assist | 20 min |
| 2 | **In-Context Analysis** — Embedded AI in Problems, Kubernetes & more | 20 min |
| 3 | **Plain English to DQL** — Natural language to powerful queries | 25 min |
| 4 | **Scaling Team Knowledge** — Troubleshooting Guides (TSGs) | 15 min |
| 5 | **Hands-On Lab & Q&A** — Guided real-world exercises | 30 min |

### Prerequisites
- Access to a Dynatrace SaaS environment
- Dynatrace Intelligence generative AI enabled (**Settings > Dynatrace Intelligence > Generative and agentic AI > Enable generative AI**)
- Permission: `ALLOW davis-copilot:dql2nl:execute;` and conversational recommender access
- Basic familiarity with the Dynatrace UI (Problems, Notebooks, Dashboards)

> **⏱ Rate Limits:** Each user can ask **25 questions** in a rolling 15-minute window. Your environment supports up to **60 questions** across all users in the same window. Pace yourselves during the lab!

---
# Module 1: The Troubleshooting Assistant — Dynatrace Assist
---

## What is Dynatrace Assist?

**Dynatrace Assist** is the global conversational AI interface inside Dynatrace. It is powered by the **Conversational Recommender** skill — one of four specialized generative AI skills.

Dynatrace Assist can:
- Answer questions about **Dynatrace configuration and usage**
- **Summarize your environment's health** (open problems, vulnerabilities, entity counts)
- Help with **onboarding** to Dynatrace features, APIs, and App development
- Provide **remediation recommendations** based on context

### How to Access Dynatrace Assist
1. Click the **Dynatrace Assist** icon (chat bubble) in the top-right corner of any Dynatrace screen.
2. A conversational panel opens where you can type natural language questions.
3. Start a **new conversation** for each new topic to improve response accuracy.

### Architecture: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
Dynatrace Intelligence uses the **RAG approach**: your prompt is enriched with relevant context (entity data, schemas, documentation) before being sent to a foundational LLM. The model does **not** learn from your data — customer data is never used to train or fine-tune any models.

### The Four Generative AI Skills

| Skill | Where | What It Does |
|-------|-------|--------------|
| **NL2DQL** | Notebooks, Dashboards (Quick Analysis) | Translates natural language → DQL queries |
| **DQL2NL** | Notebooks, Dashboards (Explain Query) | Summarizes DQL queries → plain English |
| **Conversational Recommender** | Dynatrace Assist (global + in-context) | Answers questions, summarizes, recommends |
| **Document Suggestions** | Problems app | Surfaces relevant Troubleshooting Guides for detected problems |

## Dynatrace Assist — Example Prompts by Category

### 🚀 Getting Started with Dynatrace
- *"How do I get started with sending OpenTelemetry to Dynatrace?"*
- *"What are Dynatrace workflows, and how will they improve the way I work?"*
- *"Introduce all basic DQL commands and provide examples of each one."*

### 🧠 Understanding Dynatrace Concepts
- *"What is the difference between an event and a problem in Dynatrace?"*
- *"How is the Dynatrace Security Score calculated, and why is this important?"*
- *"What are the reasons why I can't find historical data, and how can I fix this?"*

### ⚙️ Configuration Help
- *"How can I configure an SLO?"*
- *"How do I set up an alert?"*
- *"How do I set a maintenance window via API?"*

### 💻 App Development Onboarding
- *"What is the Dynatrace AppEngine and how do I get started with building my own app?"*
- *"What are the requirements for using the Dynatrace App Toolkit?"*
- *"Does Dynatrace have a design system and how can it help me build an app?"*

### 📊 Environment Data Analysis
- *"Concisely summarize all open problems, and highlight those that need immediate remediation."*
- *"Predict the future CPU usage for my hosts based on historical data."*
- *"Provide a detailed overview of the active security vulnerabilities and recommendations for remediation."*

# Module 2: In-Context Analysis — Embedded AI Conversation Starters
---

## What are Embedded Conversation Starters?

Beyond the global Dynatrace Assist panel, Dynatrace offers **embedded, context-aware AI conversations** directly within specific apps. These are predefined contextual prompts that auto-execute when clicked — the AI already has the full context of what you're viewing.

### Supported Apps and Their Capabilities

| App | Conversation Starter | What the AI Provides |
|-----|---------------------|---------------------|
| **Kubernetes** | *"Explain warning signal"* | General explanation, typical root causes (most common first), common remediation steps |
| **Problems** | *"Explain"* (single or up to 5 problems) | What happened, why it occurred, actionable remediation steps, relationship between problems |
| **Vulnerabilities** | *"Explain vulnerability"* | Description & cause, impact & exploit conditions, affected libraries/services, remediation actions |
| **Threats & Exploits** | *"Explain finding"* | Threat description, impact & likelihood, affected entities & attack paths, recommended actions |
| **Security Posture Mgmt** | *"Explain assessment"* | Rule requirements, misconfiguration details, security risks, remediation steps |
| **Databases** | *"Summarize execution plan"* | Execution plan breakdown, performance insights, optimization recommendations |
| **Dashboards** | Via `fieldsAdd prompt` in DQL | AI explanations of query results, integrated into tiles |
| **Notebooks** | Via `fieldsAdd prompt` in DQL | AI explanations of query results, integrated into sections |

### Key Advantage
You never leave your active investigation. The AI meets you **where you are**, with the context already loaded.

## Scenario A: Kubernetes Warning Signals

### Background
Your team sees warning signals on a Kubernetes workload. Pods may be experiencing OOMKilled events, CPU throttling, or unexpected scaling.

### How to Investigate with In-Context AI

1. **Navigate to the Kubernetes app** → Select any list page (Clusters, Nodes, Namespaces, or Workloads).
2. **Select any warning signal** → You'll see the option **"Explain warning signal"**.
3. Click it — **Dynatrace Assist opens automatically** and executes the predefined prompt.
4. The AI provides:
   - A **general explanation** about the event
   - **Typical root causes**, starting with the most common ones
   - **Common remediation steps** for each root cause

### What to Expect
- The AI analyzes Kubernetes events, resource metrics, and cluster state.
- It can surface OOMKilled events, CPU throttling, image pull failures, or misconfigured limits.
- Remediation suggestions may include adjusting HPA thresholds, resource requests/limits, or checking node capacity.

## Scenario B: Node.js Service Degradation & Problem Explanation

### Background
A Node.js microservice is showing increased response times and elevated failure rates. A problem has been detected by Davis.

### How to Investigate with In-Context AI

**Using the Problems App:**
1. Navigate to the **Problems** app → Open the detected problem.
2. Click **"Explain"** in the upper-right corner.
3. Dynatrace Assist opens and auto-executes. The AI provides:
   - **What happened** — a clear summary of the detected problem
   - **Why it occurred** — root cause analysis
   - **Actionable steps** to remediate the problem

**Comparing Multiple Problems:**
1. In the Problems list view, select **up to 5 problems** using the checkboxes.
2. Click **"Explain"** above the table.
3. The AI provides:
   - Individual explanation for each problem
   - **Relationship between problems** (e.g., shared root cause, dependency chain)
   - Combined remediation steps

### What to Expect
- The AI identifies whether the bottleneck is in the service, a downstream database, or an external dependency.
- It may highlight specific code-level hotspots, garbage collection issues, or deployment correlations.

## Advanced: Integrating Dynatrace Assist into Dashboard & Notebook Tiles

You can embed **Dynatrace Assist prompts directly into DQL queries** in Dashboards and Notebooks using special DQL commands.

### How It Works
Add these commands to any DQL query:
```
| fieldsAdd prompt = concat("{your question}", your.field.name)
| fieldsAdd execute = true
```

- `fieldsAdd prompt` — Defines the question to send to Dynatrace Assist
- `fieldsAdd execute = true` — Auto-executes the prompt when the user opens Assist (remove this line to let the user review/edit the prompt first)

### Adding Supplementary Context
You can pass hidden context to help the AI produce better answers:
```
| parse "{\"result\":[{\"type\":\"supplementary\", \"value\":\"The character * often represents masked data\"}]}", "LD JSON_ARRAY:contexts"
```

Or dynamically from a field:
```
| fieldsAdd supplementaryContext = concat("{\"result\":[{\"type\":\"supplementary\", \"value\":\"Use the following info: ", record.summary, "\"}]}")
| parse supplementaryContext, "LD JSON_ARRAY:contexts"
```

### To Access the Integrated Assist
1. In the query results, select the **⋯** icon next to a field entry.
2. Select **Open with… > Ask a question**.

> **Note:** This integration doesn't work with `makeTimeseries` queries.

# Module 3: Plain English to DQL (NL2DQL) & Explain Query (DQL2NL)
---

## How Natural Language to DQL Works

The **NL2DQL** skill is available in **Notebooks** and **Dashboards** via the **Quick Analysis** (prompt bar). It translates your plain English prompts into executable DQL queries.

### Where to Use It
- **Notebooks:** Click **"+"** → **Query** section → Type natural language in the prompt bar
- **Dashboards:** Add a new tile → Use the prompt bar to describe the data you want

### How the AI Generates DQL (RAG Pipeline)
1. Your natural language prompt is sent to the NL2DQL skill.
2. The prompt is enriched via **RAG** with your environment's schema (entity types, metric keys, log sources).
3. A DQL query is generated and returned for review and execution.

### The Reverse: DQL2NL (Explain Query)
Already have a complex DQL query you don't understand? Use the **"Explain query"** functionality:

**In Notebooks:**
1. Open a notebook section with a DQL query.
2. Open the **menu (⋯)** → Select **"Explain query"**.
3. A summary + detailed explanation appears below the query input.

**In Dashboards:**
1. Select a tile with a DQL query → Click **"Edit"**.
2. In the **DQL** section, select **"Explain query"**.
3. A summary + detailed explanation appears below "Run".

> **Important:** Explanations are **session-based** — they don't persist across sessions. The AI may explain line-by-line or group related lines into meaningful chunks.

> **Tip:** NL2DQL is specialized for DQL only. For general questions, use Dynatrace Assist. With **agentic AI** enabled, Assist can also call NL2DQL as a tool.

## NL2DQL Examples: Log Analysis

Here are real prompt → DQL pairs. Try typing the natural language prompt in the Quick Analysis bar and compare with the expected DQL:

| Natural Language Prompt | Expected DQL |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Show me all logs | `fetch logs` |
| Show me all log lines from the last 6 hours | `fetch logs, from:now() - 6h` |
| Chart logs by their log level over time, exclude "NONE" | `fetch logs \| filterOut loglevel == "NONE" \| makeTimeseries by:{loglevel}, interval:1h, count = count()` |
| Show me 5 log sources with the highest volume | `fetch logs \| summarize by:{log.source}, log_count = count() \| sort log_count desc \| limit 5` |
| What is causing the most error log lines? | `fetch logs, from:now()-2h \| filter loglevel == "ERROR" \| summarize by:{log.source}, errorCount = count() \| sort errorCount desc \| limit 1` |
| Compare error logs from today vs yesterday | `fetch logs, from:bin(now(),24h) \| filter loglevel == "ERROR" \| summarize todayErrorCount = count() \| append [fetch logs, from:bin(now(),24h)-24h, to:bin(now(),24h) \| filter loglevel == "ERROR" \| summarize yesterdayErrorCount = count()]` |
| Which host has the most error logs? Show host name | `fetch logs \| filter loglevel == "ERROR" \| summarize by:{dt.entity.host}, errorCount = count() \| lookup [fetch dt.entity.host \| fieldsAdd entity.name], sourceField:dt.entity.host, lookupField:id, fields:{entity.name} \| sort errorCount desc \| limit 1` |

input.value:
// 💡 Try it: Top 5 log sources by volume
fetch logs
| summarize by:{log.source}, log_count = count()
| sort log_count desc
| limit 5

// 💡 Try it: Error logs over the last 24h (hourly granularity)
fetch logs, from:now() - 24h
| filter loglevel == "ERROR"
| makeTimeseries interval:1h, count = count()

// 💡 Try it: Compare today's error logs with yesterday's
fetch logs, from:bin(now(), 24h)
| filter loglevel == "ERROR"
| summarize todayErrorCount = count()
| append
[
  fetch logs, from:bin(now(), 24h) - 24h, to:bin(now(), 24h)
  | filter loglevel == "ERROR"
  | summarize yesterdayErrorCount = count()
]

## NL2DQL Examples: Metrics & Entities

### Metrics
| Natural Language Prompt | Expected DQL |
|------------------------|-------------|
| CPU average from all K8s services by container (top 10) | `timeseries by:{k8s.container.name}, avg_cpu = avg(dt.kubernetes.container.cpu_usage) \| sort avg_cpu desc \| limit 10` |
| Compare last 24h CPU with same timeframe one week ago | `timeseries from:now()-24h, to:now(), cpu_last_24h = avg(dt.host.cpu.usage) \| append [timeseries from:now()-168h-24h, to:now()-168h, cpu_last_week = avg(dt.host.cpu.usage)]` |
| Top 10 processes by memory with their host | `timeseries by:{dt.entity.process_group_instance, dt.entity.host}, maxMem = max(dt.process.memory.working_set_size) \| summarize by:{dt.entity.process_group_instance, dt.entity.host}, maxMem = max(maxMem) \| sort maxMem desc \| limit 10` |

### Entities
| Natural Language Prompt | Expected DQL |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Azure VMs vs EC2 instances count | `fetch dt.entity.azure_vm \| summarize azure_vm_count = count() \| append [fetch dt.entity.ec2_instance \| summarize ec2_count = count()]` |
| Hosts with CPU > 60% over the last week | `timeseries by:{dt.entity.host}, from:now()-168h, cpuUsage = avg(dt.host.cpu.usage) \| filter arrayAvg(cpuUsage) > 60 \| lookup [fetch dt.entity.host], sourceField:dt.entity.host, lookupField:id` |
| 5 shortest lived Kubernetes services | `fetch dt.entity.kubernetes_service \| fieldsAdd id, entity.name, lifetime \| fieldsAdd duration = toDuration(lifetime) \| sort duration \| limit 5` |

## NL2DQL Examples: Problems & Davis Events

### Problems
| Natural Language Prompt | Expected DQL |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Problems by status for the last day as timeseries | `fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now()-24h \| makeTimeseries by:{status = event.status}, interval:1h, count = count()` |
| Top 10 problems ranked by affected entities | `fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now()-24h \| expand affected_entity_ids \| summarize by:{event.name}, affectedCount = count() \| sort affectedCount desc \| limit 10` |
| Most problem-affected entities | `fetch dt.davis.problems \| expand affected_entity_ids \| summarize by:{affected_entity_ids}, count = count() \| sort count desc` |
| Problems affecting > 500 users | `fetch dt.davis.problems \| filter dt.davis.affected_users_count > 500 \| fieldsKeep display_id, dt.davis.affected_users_count, event.category, event.description` |
| Slowdown problems in the last 3 days | `fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now()-72h \| filter event.category == "SLOWDOWN" \| summarize slowdownCount = count()` |

### Davis Events
| Natural Language Prompt | Expected DQL |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Davis events day-by-day for the last week | `fetch dt.davis.events, from:now()-168h \| fieldsAdd day = bin(timestamp, 24h) \| summarize by:{day}, event_count = count()` |
| Davis event categories summary | `fetch dt.davis.events \| summarize by:{event.category}, count = count()` |

## NL2DQL Examples: Business Events & Spans

### Business Events
| Natural Language Prompt | Expected DQL |
|------------------------|-------------|
| All business events during business hours by type and category | `fetch bizevents \| fieldsAdd day_of_week = getDayOfWeek(timestamp), hour = formatTimestamp(timestamp, format:"HH") \| filter day_of_week >= 1 AND day_of_week <= 5 AND hour >= 9 AND hour <= 17 \| summarize by:{event.type, event.category}, count()` |
| Business events over time by type | `fetch bizevents \| makeTimeseries by:{event.type}, interval:1h, count = count()` |

### Spans
| Natural Language Prompt | Expected DQL |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Average DB response time by host and database | `fetch spans \| filter span.kind == "client" AND isNotNull(db.system) AND isNotNull(server.address) AND isNotNull(db.namespace) \| summarize by:{host = server.address, database = db.namespace}, avg_duration = avg(duration)` |
| Average DB response time per minute by database type | `fetch spans \| filter span.kind == "client" AND isNotNull(db.system) \| makeTimeseries by:{db.system}, interval:1m, avg_duration = avg(duration)` |

## 📝 Best Practices for Writing NL2DQL Prompts

### ✅ DO
- **Be specific about the data source:** Mention `logs`, `metrics`, `events`, `entities`, `problems`, `bizevents`, or `spans` explicitly.
- **Specify time ranges:** *"...over the last 24 hours"*, *"...from the last week"*
- **Name the fields you want:** *"Show host name"*, *"Group by log level"*, *"Sort by count descending"*
- **Use Dynatrace vocabulary:** *"Davis events"*, *"affected entities"*, *"failure rate"*, *"response time"*
- **Request visualizations:** *"as a timeseries"*, *"as a bar chart"*, *"limit to top 10"*

### ❌ DON'T
- Don't ask general knowledge questions in Quick Analysis — use Dynatrace Assist instead
- Don't expect perfect DQL on the first try — review and refine the generated query
- Don't combine multiple unrelated analyses in a single prompt — break them into separate prompts

### 🔄 The Feedback Loop
If the AI generates an inaccurate query, use the **👍/👎 feedback** buttons directly in Notebooks or Dashboards.

# Module 4: Scaling Team Knowledge — Troubleshooting Guides (TSGs)
---

## What are Troubleshooting Guides (TSGs)?

Troubleshooting Guides are **team-authored Notebooks or Dashboards** that capture your organization's custom remediation procedures. When indexed by Dynatrace Intelligence, the AI can **automatically surface relevant TSGs** when a matching problem is detected.

### The Document Suggestions Skill
This is the fourth generative AI skill. Here's how it works:

1. **Create** a Notebook or Dashboard with your troubleshooting steps for a specific problem type.
2. **Index** the document so Dynatrace Intelligence can discover it.
3. When a matching problem occurs, the **Problems app** shows a **"Relevant Troubleshooting Guides"** section.
4. The AI uses **semantic similarity** to match the problem description with your indexed documents.

### Why This Matters
- **Onboarding:** New team members instantly find expert-written runbooks.
- **Consistency:** Everyone follows the same remediation steps.
- **Speed:** No searching wikis or Slack — the right guide surfaces automatically.
- **Institutional Knowledge:** Tribal knowledge becomes a searchable, AI-indexed asset.

## How to Create and Index a TSG

### Step 1: Create the Document
Create a new Notebook with this recommended structure:

```
Title: [Problem Type] — Troubleshooting Guide

1. Problem Description
   - What does this problem look like?
   - Common symptoms and affected entities

2. Diagnostic Steps
   - DQL queries to run (use NL2DQL to generate them!)
   - Metrics to check
   - Logs to inspect

3. Root Cause Analysis
   - Known causes for this problem type
   - How to identify each cause

4. Remediation Steps
   - Step-by-step fix instructions
   - Rollback procedures

5. Prevention
   - Configuration changes to prevent recurrence
   - Monitoring/alerting recommendations
```

### Step 2: Index for AI Discovery
1. Go to **Settings** > **Dynatrace Intelligence** > **Document Indexing**.
2. Ensure your document types (Notebooks/Dashboards) are enabled for indexing.
3. The AI will now match future problems against your indexed TSGs.

### Step 3: Validate
1. Open the **Problems** app and find a problem matching your TSG.
2. Look for the **"Relevant Troubleshooting Guides"** section.
3. Verify your document appears as a suggestion.

## ✅ Exercise 4: Build a Troubleshooting Guide

---

### Task 4.1 — Create a TSG Notebook
1. Create a **new Notebook** titled: **"High CPU Usage — Troubleshooting Guide"**
2. Add the following sections:

**Section 1 (Markdown):** Problem Description
```
## Problem: High CPU Usage on Hosts
This guide helps diagnose and resolve sustained high CPU usage (>80%) on monitored hosts.
Common symptoms: slow application response times, increased error rates, user complaints.
```

**Section 2 (DQL Query):** Use NL2DQL prompt:
*"Show all hosts with CPU usage greater than 80% over the last 24 hours with their names"*

**Section 3 (DQL Query):** Use NL2DQL prompt:
*"Show me the top 10 processes by memory consumption and the host they are running on"*

**Section 4 (Markdown):** Remediation Steps
```
## Remediation
1. Identify the top CPU-consuming process from the query above.
2. Check if a recent deployment correlates with the CPU spike.
3. If a runaway process is identified, consider restarting the service.
4. If sustained, scale horizontally or vertically.
5. Set up an alert for CPU > 85% to catch future occurrences early.
```

---

### Task 4.2 — Index the Guide
1. Save the Notebook.
2. Verify that document indexing is enabled in **Settings > Dynatrace Intelligence > Document Indexing**.
3. Discuss: What other TSGs would be valuable for your team?

---

> **💡 Key Takeaway:** TSGs convert tribal knowledge into AI-discoverable assets. The next time a matching incident occurs, the right runbook surfaces automatically.

# Module 5: Hands-On Lab — Real-World Troubleshooting Exercises
---

## Lab Overview

Combine everything from Modules 1–4 to solve realistic troubleshooting scenarios. Work individually or in pairs.

### Lab Environment
Use your provisioned Dynatrace environment with **Dynatrace Assist**, **Notebooks**, **Dashboards**, **Problems**, and **Kubernetes** apps.

### Scoring (Optional)
| Criteria | Points |
|----------|--------|
| Correct DQL query generated from NL prompt | 5 pts each |
| Meaningful use of in-context AI (Explain) | 5 pts each |
| TSG created and indexed | 10 pts |
| Creative bonus (custom prompt, novel insight) | 5 pts |

## 🧪 Lab A: Environment Health Dashboard

**Objective:** Build a comprehensive health dashboard using **only natural language prompts**.

### Instructions
1. Open **Dashboards** → Create: **"Environment Health — [Your Name]"**
2. Add tiles using NL prompts in Quick Analysis:

**Tile 1 — Active Problems:**
```
Show number of problems by problem status for the last day, as a timeseries
```

**Tile 2 — Most Affected Entities:**
```
Show most problem-affected entities
```

**Tile 3 — Error Log Trend:**
```
Show all error logs over the last day with a granularity of one hour
```

**Tile 4 — Top CPU Consumers:**
```
Show the CPU average from all Kubernetes services grouped by container name, limit to top 10
```

**Tile 5 — Davis Events Summary:**
```
Summarize how many and which categories of Davis events occurred
```

3. Review the generated DQL for each tile and adjust if needed.
4. Arrange tiles into a meaningful layout.

### ✅ Deliverable

## 🧪 Lab B: Incident Investigation Notebook

// 🧪 Lab E: Dashboard tile with embedded Dynatrace Assist
fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 24h

---
# Summary & Key Takeaways
---

## The Four AI Skills in Dynatrace Intelligence

| Skill | Where | What It Does |
|-------|-------|--------------|
| **NL2DQL** | Notebooks, Dashboards (Quick Analysis) | Translates natural language → DQL queries |
| **DQL2NL** | Notebooks, Dashboards (Explain Query) | Summarizes DQL queries → plain English |
| **Conversational Recommender** | Dynatrace Assist (global + embedded in apps) | Answers questions, summarizes, recommends |
| **Document Suggestions** | Problems app | Surfaces relevant TSGs for detected problems |

## Embedded Conversation Starters (In-Context AI)
| App | Action |
|-----|--------|
| Kubernetes | Explain warning signal |
| Problems | Explain (single or multi-select up to 5) |
| Vulnerabilities | Explain vulnerability |
| Threats & Exploits | Explain finding |
| Security Posture Mgmt | Explain assessment |
| Databases | Summarize execution plan |
| Dashboards / Notebooks | `fieldsAdd prompt` + `fieldsAdd execute` |

## Best Practices Recap
1. **Start new conversations** for new topics in Dynatrace Assist.
2. **Be specific** in NL2DQL prompts: mention data source, time range, fields, and sort order.
3. **Use in-context AI** to stay in your workflow — the AI already has the context.
4. **Create and index TSGs** to scale your team's knowledge.
5. **Always review** AI-generated DQL before acting on it — the model is probabilistic.
6. **Provide feedback** (👍/👎) to help improve the AI over time.
7. **Use `fieldsAdd prompt`** in Dashboards/Notebooks to embed Assist directly into your analysis.
